title: AI Isn’t Outthinking Mathematicians. It’s Out-Remembering Them.
excerpt: The key advantage may not be superior reasoning, but a virtually unlimited symbolic working memory.
content_html:
When an AI system solves a difficult mathematical problem, the usual explanation is that it has become more intelligent.

Perhaps it has absorbed millions of mathematical examples. Perhaps reinforcement learning has taught it better reasoning strategies. Perhaps it is beginning to develop something resembling genuine mathematical intuition.

All of these explanations may contain some truth. But they overlook a simpler possibility:

AI has access to a vastly larger working memory than the human brain.

Or, more precisely, it has access to an enormous external symbolic workspace that performs many of the functions that working memory performs in humans.

This difference may be especially important in mathematics.

A human mathematician can hold only a small number of unfamiliar elements in mind simultaneously. An AI model can keep the entire problem statement, hundreds of intermediate equations, several abandoned approaches, definitions, constraints and earlier conclusions inside its context window.

We normally interpret the resulting performance as evidence of superior reasoning. But some of it may instead reflect the removal of one of the most important biological limits on human reasoning: our extremely restricted working-memory capacity.

Working memory is the mental system that allows us to hold and manipulate information over short periods.

When solving an equation, you must remember what each variable represents, which operations have already been performed and what the current goal is. During a proof, you may need to keep track of assumptions, intermediate lemmas, exceptions and multiple possible cases.

Human working memory is remarkably limited.

Its exact capacity depends on the task and on how information is organized, but the general limitation is obvious from everyday experience. Try multiplying two three-digit numbers in your head. The underlying operations are simple. The difficulty comes largely from having to preserve partial results while performing additional calculations.

Writing the numbers down transforms the problem.

Paper does not make you more intelligent. It expands your effective working memory.

The same principle applies at higher levels of mathematics. A mathematician uses notation, scratch paper, diagrams and previously written lemmas not merely to communicate the solution, but to make the reasoning cognitively possible.

Experts compensate through “chunking.” A novice sees a long sequence of symbols. An expert recognizes a familiar structure and treats it as a single conceptual object. This allows far more information to fit inside the same biological working-memory limit.

But chunking does not eliminate the limit. It merely compresses the information.

An AI model faces a very different constraint.

The importance of working memory for mathematics is not merely theoretical. It is visible in the differences between human beings.

Working memory is strongly related to general intelligence, which raises an obvious question: does it independently predict mathematical performance, or is it merely another imperfect measure of IQ?

Several studies suggest that it contributes something beyond conventional intelligence measures. Alloway and Passolunghi (2011), for example, examined working memory, verbal ability and mathematical skills in children. They found that working-memory measures made a distinct contribution to mathematical performance rather than simply reproducing the association between mathematics and general verbal ability.

In a separate six-year longitudinal study, Alloway and Alloway (2010) measured children at age five and then examined their academic achievement six years later. Early working-memory performance predicted later literacy and numeracy even after IQ was included in the analysis. Indeed, working memory was a stronger predictor of the later academic outcomes than the IQ measure used in the study.

Blankenship and colleagues (2015) similarly reported that working memory explained unique variation in mathematical fluency and calculation after statistically controlling for IQ and age. A large meta-analysis by Friso-van den Bos and colleagues (2013) also found a consistent relationship between working memory and mathematics across primary-school studies, although the strength of the relationship varied according to the type of working-memory and mathematical task being measured.

These findings should not be exaggerated. Working memory and intelligence overlap substantially, and statistical control cannot perfectly isolate them as independent psychological mechanisms. Nor does the evidence imply that commercially training working memory will necessarily produce large improvements in intelligence or mathematics.

The narrower conclusion is nevertheless important: among children with similar measured intelligence, differences in the ability to hold, update and manipulate information still predict differences in mathematical performance.

This provides a crucial clue for understanding AI. If human mathematical performance is partly capped by a working-memory bottleneck, then giving a machine an enormous symbolic workspace changes the nature of the contest. The machine may appear more mathematically intelligent partly because it is much less constrained by a cognitive limitation that suppresses human performance.

A modern language model can process an enormous sequence of tokens at once. This sequence may include the original question, definitions, examples, intermediate calculations and the model’s own earlier reasoning.

The context window is not identical to human working memory. It is better understood as a gigantic external notebook combined with an imperfect system for searching and using what has been written in it.

This distinction matters.

Humans possess a form of active internal memory. We can silently choose a number, hold it in mind, transform it and replace it with a new value without saying or writing anything.

Standard language models are much weaker at maintaining this kind of private, continuously updated mental state. Their most stable form of memory is usually the sequence of tokens that has already been generated.

If the model writes:

x=6

and later writes:

x+3=9,

those statements remain inside the context. The model can attend to them again when generating the next step.

Its reasoning is therefore often externalized. The text is not merely a report of a completed thought process. The text is part of the mechanism by which the reasoning occurs.

Humans do something similar when using scratch paper. The major difference is scale.

An unaided human may struggle to keep five unfamiliar conditions active simultaneously. An AI can preserve dozens or hundreds of them in explicit form.

This does not mean that every item in a long context is retrieved perfectly. Models can overlook relevant information, become distracted or lose track of details. Advertised context length is not the same as perfectly usable memory.

Nevertheless, the difference in potential capacity is enormous.

The context-window advantage is not equally useful in every kind of reasoning.

It matters especially for mathematics because mathematical reasoning can be translated unusually well into explicit symbols.

Almost every relevant element of a mathematical problem can be written down:

  • the assumptions;

  • the definitions;

  • the known equations;

  • the current objective;

  • the results already proved;

  • the cases that have been eliminated;

  • the conditions under which each step remains valid.

Once written, this information remains stable.

If (x) is defined as an integer at the beginning of a proof, it remains an integer unless the proof explicitly changes the definition. A strict inequality does not gradually become a non-strict inequality because of changes in mood, context or interpretation.

Mathematical symbols are designed to reduce ambiguity.

This makes mathematics almost perfectly suited to an intelligence that operates through a large textual workspace.

Consider a problem requiring the solver to remember that:

  • n is odd;

  • p is prime;

  • x≠0

and that one branch of the argument has already produced a contradiction.

A human may understand the basic strategy but divide by x before establishing that x≠0. The error is not necessarily caused by a lack of intelligence. It may be a failure of bookkeeping.

An AI can restate the active constraints at each stage:

We are working under the assumptions that (n) is odd, (p) is prime and (x≠0).

The context becomes a ledger of the reasoning state.

Many difficult mathematical problems contain a profound insight somewhere near the beginning, but they also contain a large amount of less glamorous work afterward: expanding expressions, checking cases, carrying conditions through transformations and making sure that the final conclusion is compatible with every earlier assumption.

A machine does not need to possess deeper insight than a human to gain an advantage here. It may simply be better equipped to preserve the entire state of the problem while completing a long sequence of operations.

Mathematics is highly compositional.

A proof can often be represented as:

A → B → C → D

If each step is valid and the chain is preserved accurately, the conclusion follows.

A large working space allows the model to construct much longer chains before losing the thread.

This is important because the difficulty of a problem does not depend only on the difficulty of each individual step. It also depends on how many steps must be coordinated.

A person may be perfectly capable of understanding every local inference in a 100-step argument while still being unable to generate the entire argument unaided. The problem exceeds the person’s ability to maintain the global structure.

AI can potentially compensate by writing down nearly everything.

This may explain why additional “thinking time” often improves model performance. More computation allows the system to produce more intermediate states, examine alternative branches and preserve partial conclusions.

What looks like deeper thought may sometimes be broader search conducted inside a much larger notebook.

Now compare a mathematical problem with a social question:

Why has Maria suddenly stopped replying to my messages?

A larger context window might allow an AI to examine years of correspondence. It could identify changes in tone, timing and vocabulary.

But the decisive information may still be missing.

Perhaps Maria is angry. Perhaps she is busy. Perhaps she is ill. Perhaps she has lost her phone. Perhaps she is avoiding an unrelated problem.

No amount of memory can retrieve facts that were never observed.

The challenge is not simply to preserve a known set of premises and derive their consequences. It is to reason under uncertainty about hidden causes.

Informal reasoning also depends heavily on concepts whose meanings are unstable.

Words such as “fair,” “successful,” “responsible,” “harmful” or “intelligent” do not possess the exactness of mathematical variables. Their meaning depends on culture, goals and context.

A model can remember every sentence in a discussion while still misunderstanding what the participants mean.

The same applies to political analysis, historical interpretation, business strategy and psychological judgment. In these domains, the central problem is often not working-memory capacity. It is identifying the correct causal model when the evidence is incomplete and ambiguous.

A larger notebook helps, but it does not solve the fundamental problem.

Mathematics is different because the reasoning environment is artificially constructed to make assumptions explicit and transformations verifiable.

Mathematical answers can often be checked.

A solution to an equation can be substituted back into the original expression. A proposed identity can be evaluated numerically. A computer program can test hundreds of cases. A formal proof assistant can verify whether every inference follows from accepted rules.

This creates an ideal environment for AI.

The model can use its context not only to produce a solution but also to record alternative approaches, identify contradictions and correct previous mistakes.

In less formal domains, feedback is much weaker.

A persuasive historical explanation may be impossible to verify conclusively. A business strategy may not reveal whether it was correct until years later. A psychological interpretation may remain permanently uncertain.

In such fields, a long and coherent argument can still be completely wrong.

Mathematics rewards systems that can generate, store and verify explicit intermediate states. These are precisely the abilities that context windows, scratchpads, code execution and formal verification amplify.

Some researchers would object to describing a context window as working memory.

They have a point.

Human working memory is not merely a storage buffer. It involves attention, inhibition, continuous updating and the active manipulation of internal representations.

A language model’s context is more passive. Previous tokens remain fixed. The model cannot literally return to an earlier line and replace it. It generates new tokens conditioned on the existing record.

The most accurate description may therefore be augmented symbolic working memory.

The model has weaker private mental memory than a human in some respects, but vastly greater explicit memory in others.

Humans are better at silently maintaining a small internal state. AI is better at operating over an enormous written record.

For mathematics, the second ability may often be more valuable.

Formal reasoning does not require every relevant state to remain private. On the contrary, mathematics improves when assumptions and intermediate steps are made explicit.

The apparent weakness of AI—its tendency to “think out loud”—becomes an advantage when the domain itself is built from written symbols.

This leads to a broader question: what does it mean to say that AI is “better at mathematics” than humans?

Imagine giving two people the same mathematical problem.

One must solve it entirely in their head. The other receives unlimited paper, perfect notes, instant access to every previous calculation, the ability to try several approaches in parallel and a machine that checks each result.

If the second person wins, we would not necessarily conclude that the second person possesses greater raw mathematical intelligence. We might instead conclude that the second person had a much better cognitive architecture for the task.

The same caution should apply when comparing humans and AI.

AI systems are trained on enormous quantities of mathematical material. They can generate many possible solutions, use code, consult tools and preserve long reasoning traces.

Their performance is therefore the product of several factors: mathematical knowledge, reasoning ability, memory capacity, search, and verification.

We tend to focus on reasoning because it is the most philosophically exciting component. But memory may be doing much more of the work than we realize.

The working-memory hypothesis produces clear predictions.

AI’s advantage should be largest on problems that involve:

  • many interacting constraints;

  • long calculations;

  • extensive case analysis;

  • repeated reference to previous results;

  • exact symbolic bookkeeping;

  • large bodies of formal definitions.

Its advantage should be smaller on problems that depend primarily on one short conceptual leap.

A brilliant mathematician may still outperform AI when the crucial challenge is finding an entirely new representation of a problem. Once that representation has been found, however, AI may be superior at exploring all its consequences.

The hypothesis also predicts that reducing a model’s usable context or preventing it from writing intermediate steps should disproportionately damage performance on long mathematical tasks.

Conversely, expanding a human’s external memory—with clear notation, diagrams, software and structured notes—should narrow part of the gap.

The fairest comparison may therefore not be AI against a human thinking unaided. It may be AI with its tools against a human with equally powerful external memory and verification systems.

The rise of mathematical AI is often described as a triumph of machine intelligence over human intelligence.

That interpretation may be premature.

AI certainly appears to be learning better reasoning strategies. It may eventually develop forms of mathematical intuition that equal or exceed our own.

But some of its present advantage may be more prosaic.

The human brain evolved under severe constraints. It has limited working memory, becomes tired, loses intermediate results and struggles to coordinate long chains of unfamiliar symbols.

AI is not bound by the same architecture.

It can turn reasoning into text and use that text as a vast external cognitive workspace. Mathematics, because of its precision and symbolic structure, is the domain where this advantage is most easily converted into superior performance.

The real reason AI is beating humans at mathematics may therefore be less mysterious than we imagine.

Perhaps the most revealing comparison is not between AI and the average human, but between two very different forms of genius.

The physicist Eugene Wigner, who knew both John von Neumann and Albert Einstein, wrote that no one he had encountered possessed a mind as “quick and acute” as von Neumann’s. Von Neumann could absorb vast amounts of information, follow extraordinarily complicated arguments and move between mathematical fields with astonishing speed. Yet Wigner still regarded Einstein’s understanding as deeper, more penetrating and more original. Von Neumann may have had the greater raw intellectual processing capacity, but Einstein was more likely to reconceptualize the problem itself.

Present-day AI appears more like a machine-amplified version of the first set of abilities than the second. It is extraordinarily fast, broad and capable of preserving and manipulating huge quantities of explicit information. It can search many possibilities, remember long chains of deductions and execute formal reasoning at a scale no unaided human can match. But that does not necessarily mean it possesses Einsteinian depth: the ability to discard the accepted framework, identify the hidden conceptual error and invent a radically new way of seeing reality.

The analogy should not be pushed too far. Von Neumann was himself an immensely original thinker, not merely a fast calculator. But Wigner’s distinction captures something important. AI may currently be beating humans at mathematics less by thinking like Einstein than by combining something resembling von Neumann’s speed and breadth with a practically unlimited notebook.

The next great threshold will be reached when AI can do more than solve existing problems faster than humans. It will be reached when AI can recognize that a problem has been framed incorrectly and invent a fundamentally better way of understanding it.

sentences.zh: 当人工智能系统解决了一个困难的数学问题时，通常的解释是它变得更加聪明。

blocks.html_en: Perhaps it has absorbed millions of mathematical examples. Perhaps reinforcement learning has taught it better reasoning strategies. Perhaps it is beginning to develop something resembling genuine mathematical intuition.

sentences.en: Perhaps it has absorbed millions of mathematical examples.
sentences.zh: 也许它吸收了数以百万计的数学例子。

sentences.en: Perhaps reinforcement learning has taught it better reasoning strategies.
sentences.zh: 也许强化学习教会了它更好的推理策略。

sentences.en: Perhaps it is beginning to develop something resembling genuine mathematical intuition.
sentences.zh: 也许它正在开始发展出类似真正数学直觉的东西。

blocks.html_en: All of these explanations may contain some truth. But they overlook a simpler possibility:

sentences.en: All of these explanations may contain some truth.
sentences.zh: 所有这些解释可能都有一定道理。

sentences.en: But they overlook a simpler possibility:
sentences.zh: 但他们忽略了一个更简单的可能性：

blocks.html_en: AI has access to a vastly larger working memory than the human brain.

sentences.en: AI has access to a vastly larger working memory than the human brain.
sentences.zh: 人工智能拥有比人脑大得多的工作记忆。

blocks.html_en: Or, more precisely, it has access to an enormous external symbolic workspace that performs many of the functions that working memory performs in humans.

sentences.en: Or, more precisely, it has access to an enormous external symbolic workspace that performs many of the functions that working memory performs in humans.
sentences.zh: 或者，更准确地说，它可以访问巨大的外部符号工作空间，该工作空间执行人类工作记忆执行的许多功能。

blocks.html_en: This difference may be especially important in mathematics.

sentences.en: This difference may be especially important in mathematics.
sentences.zh: 这种差异在数学中可能尤其重要。

blocks.html_en: A human mathematician can hold only a small number of unfamiliar elements in mind simultaneously. An AI model can keep the entire problem statement, hundreds of intermediate equations, several abandoned approaches, definitions, constraints and earlier conclusions inside its context window.

sentences.en: A human mathematician can hold only a small number of unfamiliar elements in mind simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 人类数学家只能同时记住少量不熟悉的元素。

sentences.en: An AI model can keep the entire problem statement, hundreds of intermediate equations, several abandoned approaches, definitions, constraints and earlier conclusions inside its context window.
sentences.zh: 人工智能模型可以将整个问题陈述、数百个中间方程、几种废弃的方法、定义、约束和早期结论保留在其上下文窗口内。

blocks.html_en: We normally interpret the resulting performance as evidence of superior reasoning. But some of it may instead reflect the removal of one of the most important biological limits on human reasoning: our extremely restricted working-memory capacity.

sentences.en: We normally interpret the resulting performance as evidence of superior reasoning.
sentences.zh: 我们通常将由此产生的表现解释为卓越推理的证据。

sentences.en: But some of it may instead reflect the removal of one of the most important biological limits on human reasoning: our extremely restricted working-memory capacity.
sentences.zh: 但其中一些可能反而反映了人类推理最重要的生物学限制之一的消除：我们极其有限的工作记忆能力。

blocks.html_en: Working memory is the mental system that allows us to hold and manipulate information over short periods.

sentences.en: Working memory is the mental system that allows us to hold and manipulate information over short periods.
sentences.zh: 工作记忆是一种心理系统，使我们能够在短时间内保存和操纵信息。

blocks.html_en: When solving an equation, you must remember what each variable represents, which operations have already been performed and what the current goal is. During a proof, you may need to keep track of assumptions, intermediate lemmas, exceptions and multiple possible cases.

sentences.en: When solving an equation, you must remember what each variable represents, which operations have already been performed and what the current goal is.
sentences.zh: 解方程时，必须记住每个变量代表什么，已经执行了哪些操作以及当前目标是什么。

sentences.en: During a proof, you may need to keep track of assumptions, intermediate lemmas, exceptions and multiple possible cases.
sentences.zh: 在证明过程中，您可能需要跟踪假设、中间引理、例外和多种可能的情况。

blocks.html_en: Human working memory is remarkably limited.

sentences.en: Human working memory is remarkably limited.
sentences.zh: 人类的工作记忆非常有限。

blocks.html_en: Its exact capacity depends on the task and on how information is organized, but the general limitation is obvious from everyday experience. Try multiplying two three-digit numbers in your head. The underlying operations are simple. The difficulty comes largely from having to preserve partial results while performing additional calculations.

sentences.en: Its exact capacity depends on the task and on how information is organized, but the general limitation is obvious from everyday experience.
sentences.zh: 它的确切容量取决于任务和信息的组织方式，但从日常经验来看，一般限制是显而易见的。

sentences.en: Try multiplying two three-digit numbers in your head.
sentences.zh: 尝试在头脑中将两个三位数相乘。

sentences.en: The underlying operations are simple.
sentences.zh: 底层操作很简单。

sentences.en: The difficulty comes largely from having to preserve partial results while performing additional calculations.
sentences.zh: 困难主要来自于在执行额外计算时必须保留部分结果。

blocks.html_en: Writing the numbers down transforms the problem.

sentences.en: Writing the numbers down transforms the problem.
sentences.zh: 把数字写下来可以改变问题。

blocks.html_en: Paper does not make you more intelligent. It expands your effective working memory.

sentences.en: Paper does not make you more intelligent.
sentences.zh: 纸并不会让你变得更聪明。

sentences.en: It expands your effective working memory.
sentences.zh: 它可以扩展您的有效工作记忆。

blocks.html_en: The same principle applies at higher levels of mathematics. A mathematician uses notation, scratch paper, diagrams and previously written lemmas not merely to communicate the solution, but to make the reasoning cognitively possible.

sentences.en: The same principle applies at higher levels of mathematics.
sentences.zh: 同样的原理也适用于更高层次的数学。

sentences.en: A mathematician uses notation, scratch paper, diagrams and previously written lemmas not merely to communicate the solution, but to make the reasoning cognitively possible.
sentences.zh: 数学家使用符号、草稿纸、图表和先前写下的引理不仅是为了传达解决方案，而且是为了使推理在认知上成为可能。

blocks.html_en: Experts compensate through “chunking.” A novice sees a long sequence of symbols. An expert recognizes a familiar structure and treats it as a single conceptual object. This allows far more information to fit inside the same biological working-memory limit.

sentences.en: Experts compensate through “chunking.”
sentences.zh: 专家通过“分块”进行补偿。

sentences.en: A novice sees a long sequence of symbols.
sentences.zh: 新手看到一长串符号。

sentences.en: An expert recognizes a familiar structure and treats it as a single conceptual object.
sentences.zh: 专家会识别熟悉的结构并将其视为单个概念对象。

sentences.en: This allows far more information to fit inside the same biological working-memory limit.
sentences.zh: 这使得在相同的生物工作记忆限制内可以容纳更多的信息。

blocks.html_en: But chunking does not eliminate the limit. It merely compresses the information.

sentences.en: But chunking does not eliminate the limit.
sentences.zh: 但分块并不能消除限制。

sentences.en: It merely compresses the information.
sentences.zh: 它只是压缩信息。

blocks.html_en: An AI model faces a very different constraint.

sentences.en: An AI model faces a very different constraint.
sentences.zh: 人工智能模型面临着截然不同的约束。

blocks.html_en: The importance of working memory for mathematics is not merely theoretical. It is visible in the differences between human beings.

sentences.en: The importance of working memory for mathematics is not merely theoretical.
sentences.zh: 工作记忆对于数学的重要性不仅仅是理论上的。

sentences.en: It is visible in the differences between human beings.
sentences.zh: 从人与人之间的差异就可以看出。

blocks.html_en: Working memory is strongly related to general intelligence, which raises an obvious question: does it independently predict mathematical performance, or is it merely another imperfect measure of IQ?

sentences.en: Working memory is strongly related to general intelligence, which raises an obvious question: does it independently predict mathematical performance, or is it merely another imperfect measure of IQ?
sentences.zh: 工作记忆与一般智力密切相关，这提出了一个明显的问题：它是否独立预测数学表现，或者仅仅是智商的另一种不完美的衡量标准？

blocks.html_en: Several studies suggest that it contributes something beyond conventional intelligence measures. Alloway and Passolunghi (2011), for example, examined working memory, verbal ability and mathematical skills in children. They found that working-memory measures made a distinct contribution to mathematical performance rather than simply reproducing the association between mathematics and general verbal ability.

sentences.en: Several studies suggest that it contributes something beyond conventional intelligence measures.
sentences.zh: 多项研究表明，它的贡献超出了传统的情报措施。

sentences.en: Alloway and Passolunghi (2011), for example, examined working memory, verbal ability and mathematical skills in children.
sentences.zh: 例如，Alloway 和 Passolunghi (2011) 检查了儿童的工作记忆、语言能力和数学技能。

sentences.en: They found that working-memory measures made a distinct contribution to mathematical performance rather than simply reproducing the association between mathematics and general verbal ability.
sentences.zh: 他们发现工作记忆测量对数学表现做出了明显的贡献，而不是简单地再现数学和一般语言能力之间的关联。

blocks.html_en: In a separate six-year longitudinal study, Alloway and Alloway (2010) measured children at age five and then examined their academic achievement six years later. Early working-memory performance predicted later literacy and numeracy even after IQ was included in the analysis. Indeed, working memory was a stronger predictor of the later academic outcomes than the IQ measure used in the study.

sentences.en: In a separate six-year longitudinal study, Alloway and Alloway (2010) measured children at age five and then examined their academic achievement six years later.
sentences.zh: 在一项单独的为期六年的纵向研究中，阿洛韦和阿洛韦（2010）测量了五岁时的儿童，然后在六年后检查了他们的学业成绩。

sentences.en: Early working-memory performance predicted later literacy and numeracy even after IQ was included in the analysis.
sentences.zh: 即使在分析中纳入了智商之后，早期的工作记忆表现也能预测后来的识字和算术能力。

sentences.en: Indeed, working memory was a stronger predictor of the later academic outcomes than the IQ measure used in the study.
sentences.zh: 事实上，工作记忆比研究中使用的智商测量更能预测后期的学业成绩。

blocks.html_en: Blankenship and colleagues (2015) similarly reported that working memory explained unique variation in mathematical fluency and calculation after statistically controlling for IQ and age. A large meta-analysis by Friso-van den Bos and colleagues (2013) also found a consistent relationship between working memory and mathematics across primary-school studies, although the strength of the relationship varied according to the type of working-memory and mathematical task being measured.

sentences.en: Blankenship and colleagues (2015) similarly reported that working memory explained unique variation in mathematical fluency and calculation after statistically controlling for IQ and age.
sentences.zh: Blankenship 及其同事（2015）类似地报告说，在统计控制智商和年龄后，工作记忆解释了数学流畅性和计算的独特变化。

sentences.en: A large meta-analysis by Friso-van den Bos and colleagues (2013) also found a consistent relationship between working memory and mathematics across primary-school studies, although the strength of the relationship varied according to the type of working-memory and mathematical task being measured.
sentences.zh: Friso-van den Bos 及其同事（2013）进行的一项大型荟萃分析也发现，小学研究中的工作记忆和数学之间存在一致的关系，尽管这种关系的强度根据工作记忆和所测量的数学任务的类型而有所不同。

blocks.html_en: These findings should not be exaggerated. Working memory and intelligence overlap substantially, and statistical control cannot perfectly isolate them as independent psychological mechanisms. Nor does the evidence imply that commercially training working memory will necessarily produce large improvements in intelligence or mathematics.

sentences.en: These findings should not be exaggerated.
sentences.zh: 这些发现不应被夸大。

sentences.en: Working memory and intelligence overlap substantially, and statistical control cannot perfectly isolate them as independent psychological mechanisms.
sentences.zh: 工作记忆和智力有很大重叠，统计控制无法将它们完美地隔离为独立的心理机制。

sentences.en: Nor does the evidence imply that commercially training working memory will necessarily produce large improvements in intelligence or mathematics.
sentences.zh: 证据也不意味着商业训练工作记忆一定会带来智力或数学的巨大进步。

blocks.html_en: The narrower conclusion is nevertheless important: among children with similar measured intelligence, differences in the ability to hold, update and manipulate information still predict differences in mathematical performance.

sentences.en: The narrower conclusion is nevertheless important: among children with similar measured intelligence, differences in the ability to hold, update and manipulate information still predict differences in mathematical performance.
sentences.zh: 然而，狭义的结论仍然很重要：在具有相似测量智力的儿童中，掌握、更新和操纵信息的能力的差异仍然预示着数学表现的差异。

blocks.html_en: This provides a crucial clue for understanding AI. If human mathematical performance is partly capped by a working-memory bottleneck, then giving a machine an enormous symbolic workspace changes the nature of the contest. The machine may appear more mathematically intelligent partly because it is much less constrained by a cognitive limitation that suppresses human performance.

sentences.en: This provides a crucial clue for understanding AI.
sentences.zh: 这为理解人工智能提供了重要线索。

sentences.en: If human mathematical performance is partly capped by a working-memory bottleneck, then giving a machine an enormous symbolic workspace changes the nature of the contest.
sentences.zh: 如果人类的数学表现在一定程度上受到工作记忆瓶颈的限制，那么为机器提供巨大的符号工作空间就会改变比赛的性质。

sentences.en: The machine may appear more mathematically intelligent partly because it is much less constrained by a cognitive limitation that suppresses human performance.
sentences.zh: 机器在数学上可能显得更加智能，部分原因是它较少受到抑制人类表现的认知限制的约束。

blocks.html_en: A modern language model can process an enormous sequence of tokens at once. This sequence may include the original question, definitions, examples, intermediate calculations and the model’s own earlier reasoning.

sentences.en: A modern language model can process an enormous sequence of tokens at once.
sentences.zh: 现代语言模型可以同时处理大量的标记序列。

sentences.en: This sequence may include the original question, definitions, examples, intermediate calculations and the model’s own earlier reasoning.
sentences.zh: 该序列可能包括原始问题、定义、示例、中间计算和模型自己的早期推理。

blocks.html_en: The context window is not identical to human working memory. It is better understood as a gigantic external notebook combined with an imperfect system for searching and using what has been written in it.

sentences.en: The context window is not identical to human working memory.
sentences.zh: 上下文窗口与人类工作记忆不同。

sentences.en: It is better understood as a gigantic external notebook combined with an imperfect system for searching and using what has been written in it.
sentences.zh: 更好地理解它是一个巨大的外部笔记本，加上一个不完善的搜索和使用其中所写内容的系统。

blocks.html_en: This distinction matters.

sentences.en: This distinction matters.
sentences.zh: 这种区别很重要。

blocks.html_en: Humans possess a form of active internal memory. We can silently choose a number, hold it in mind, transform it and replace it with a new value without saying or writing anything.

sentences.en: Humans possess a form of active internal memory.
sentences.zh: 人类拥有一种活跃的内部记忆。

sentences.en: We can silently choose a number, hold it in mind, transform it and replace it with a new value without saying or writing anything.
sentences.zh: 我们可以默默地选择一个数字，将其牢记在心，对其进行转换并用新值替换它，而无需说或写任何内容。

blocks.html_en: Standard language models are much weaker at maintaining this kind of private, continuously updated mental state. Their most stable form of memory is usually the sequence of tokens that has already been generated.

sentences.en: Standard language models are much weaker at maintaining this kind of private, continuously updated mental state.
sentences.zh: 标准语言模型在维持这种私密的、不断更新的心理状态方面要弱得多。

sentences.en: Their most stable form of memory is usually the sequence of tokens that has already been generated.
sentences.zh: 它们最稳定的记忆形式通常是已经生成的标记序列。

blocks.html_en: Humans do something similar when using scratch paper. The major difference is scale.

sentences.en: Humans do something similar when using scratch paper.
sentences.zh: 人类在使用草稿纸时也会做类似的事情。

sentences.en: The major difference is scale.

blocks.html_en: An unaided human may struggle to keep five unfamiliar conditions active simultaneously. An AI can preserve dozens or hundreds of them in explicit form.

sentences.en: An unaided human may struggle to keep five unfamiliar conditions active simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 一个没有帮助的人可能很难同时保持五个不熟悉的条件处于活动状态。

sentences.en: An AI can preserve dozens or hundreds of them in explicit form.
sentences.zh: 人工智能可以以明确的形式保存数十或数百个它们。

blocks.html_en: This does not mean that every item in a long context is retrieved perfectly. Models can overlook relevant information, become distracted or lose track of details. Advertised context length is not the same as perfectly usable memory.

sentences.en: This does not mean that every item in a long context is retrieved perfectly.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着长上下文中的每个项目都可以完美检索。

sentences.en: Models can overlook relevant information, become distracted or lose track of details.
sentences.zh: 模型可能会忽略相关信息、分心或忘记细节。

sentences.en: Advertised context length is not the same as perfectly usable memory.
sentences.zh: 公布的上下文长度与完全可用的内存不同。

blocks.html_en: Nevertheless, the difference in potential capacity is enormous.

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the difference in potential capacity is enormous.
sentences.zh: 然而，潜在能力的差异是巨大的。

sentences.en: The context-window advantage is not equally useful in every kind of reasoning.
sentences.zh: 上下文窗口的优势并非在每种推理中都同样有用。

blocks.html_en: We are working under the assumptions that (n) is odd, (p) is prime and (x≠0).

sentences.en: We are working under the assumptions that (n) is odd, (p) is prime and (x≠0).
sentences.zh: 我们假设 (n) 为奇数、(p) 为素数且 (x≠0)。

blocks.html_en: The context becomes a ledger of the reasoning state.

sentences.en: The context becomes a ledger of the reasoning state.
sentences.zh: 上下文成为推理状态的分类账。

blocks.html_en: Many difficult mathematical problems contain a profound insight somewhere near the beginning, but they also contain a large amount of less glamorous work afterward: expanding expressions, checking cases, carrying conditions through transformations and making sure that the final conclusion is compatible with every earlier assumption.

sentences.en: Many difficult mathematical problems contain a profound insight somewhere near the beginning, but they also contain a large amount of less glamorous work afterward: expanding expressions, checking cases, carrying conditions through transformations and making sure that the final conclusion is compatible with every earlier assumption.
sentences.zh: 许多困难的数学问题在开始时就包含了深刻的见解，但随后也包含了大量不那么光鲜亮丽的工作：扩展表达式、检查案例、通过转换携带条件以及确保最终结论与每个早期假设兼容。

blocks.html_en: A machine does not need to possess deeper insight than a human to gain an advantage here. It may simply be better equipped to preserve the entire state of the problem while completing a long sequence of operations.

sentences.en: A machine does not need to possess deeper insight than a human to gain an advantage here.
sentences.zh: 机器不需要比人类拥有更深刻的洞察力来获得优势。

sentences.en: It may simply be better equipped to preserve the entire state of the problem while completing a long sequence of operations.
sentences.zh: 它可能只是在完成一长串操作的同时能够更好地保留问题的整个状态。

blocks.html_en: Mathematics is highly compositional.

sentences.en: Mathematics is highly compositional.
sentences.zh: 数学是高度综合性的。

blocks.html_en: A proof can often be represented as:

sentences.en: A proof can often be represented as:
sentences.zh: 证明通常可以表示为：

blocks.html_en: A → B → C → D
If each step is valid and the chain is preserved accurately, the conclusion follows.

sentences.en: If each step is valid and the chain is preserved accurately, the conclusion follows.
sentences.zh: 如果每一步都是有效的并且链条被准确保存，那么结论如下。

blocks.html_en: A large working space allows the model to construct much longer chains before losing the thread.

sentences.en: A large working space allows the model to construct much longer chains before losing the thread.
sentences.zh: 较大的工作空间允许模型在丢失线程之前构建更长的链。

blocks.html_en: This is important because the difficulty of a problem does not depend only on the difficulty of each individual step. It also depends on how many steps must be coordinated.

sentences.en: This is important because the difficulty of a problem does not depend only on the difficulty of each individual step.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为问题的难度不仅仅取决于每个步骤的难度。

sentences.en: It also depends on how many steps must be coordinated.
sentences.zh: 它还取决于必须协调多少步骤。

blocks.html_en: A person may be perfectly capable of understanding every local inference in a 100-step argument while still being unable to generate the entire argument unaided. The problem exceeds the person’s ability to maintain the global structure.

sentences.en: A person may be perfectly capable of understanding every local inference in a 100-step argument while still being unable to generate the entire argument unaided.
sentences.zh: 一个人可能完全有能力理解 100 步论证中的每一个局部推论，但仍然无法在没有帮助的情况下生成整个论证。

sentences.en: The problem exceeds the person’s ability to maintain the global structure.
sentences.zh: 这个问题超出了人维持全局结构的能力。

blocks.html_en: AI can potentially compensate by writing down nearly everything.

sentences.en: AI can potentially compensate by writing down nearly everything.
sentences.zh: 人工智能可以通过写下几乎所有东西来进行潜在的补偿。

blocks.html_en: This may explain why additional “thinking time” often improves model performance. More computation allows the system to produce more intermediate states, examine alternative branches and preserve partial conclusions.

sentences.en: This may explain why additional “thinking time” often improves model performance.
sentences.zh: 这可以解释为什么额外的“思考时间”通常会提高模型性能。

sentences.en: More computation allows the system to produce more intermediate states, examine alternative branches and preserve partial conclusions.
sentences.zh: 更多的计算允许系统产生更多的中间状态，检查替代分支并保留部分结论。

blocks.html_en: What looks like deeper thought may sometimes be broader search conducted inside a much larger notebook.

sentences.en: What looks like deeper thought may sometimes be broader search conducted inside a much larger notebook.
sentences.zh: 看似更深层次的思考有时可能是在更大的笔记本中进行的更广泛的搜索。

blocks.html_en: Now compare a mathematical problem with a social question:

sentences.en: Now compare a mathematical problem with a social question:
sentences.zh: 现在将数学问题与社会问题进行比较：

blocks.html_en: Why has Maria suddenly stopped replying to my messages?

sentences.en: Why has Maria suddenly stopped replying to my messages?
sentences.zh: 为什么玛丽亚突然不再回复我的消息了？

blocks.html_en: Why has Maria suddenly stopped replying to my messages?

sentences.en: Why has Maria suddenly stopped replying to my messages?
sentences.zh: 为什么玛丽亚突然不再回复我的消息了？

blocks.html_en: A larger context window might allow an AI to examine years of correspondence. It could identify changes in tone, timing and vocabulary.

sentences.en: A larger context window might allow an AI to examine years of correspondence.
sentences.zh: 更大的上下文窗口可能允许人工智能检查多年的通信。

sentences.en: It could identify changes in tone, timing and vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 它可以识别语气、时间和词汇的变化。

blocks.html_en: But the decisive information may still be missing.

sentences.en: But the decisive information may still be missing.
sentences.zh: 但决定性的信息可能仍然缺失。

blocks.html_en: Perhaps Maria is angry. Perhaps she is busy. Perhaps she is ill. Perhaps she has lost her phone. Perhaps she is avoiding an unrelated problem.

sentences.en: Perhaps Maria is angry.
sentences.zh: 也许玛丽亚很生气。

sentences.en: Perhaps she is busy.
sentences.zh: 也许她很忙。

sentences.en: Perhaps she is ill.
sentences.zh: 也许她病了。

sentences.en: Perhaps she has lost her phone.
sentences.zh: 也许她丢了手机。

sentences.en: Perhaps she is avoiding an unrelated problem.
sentences.zh: 也许她是在回避一个不相关的问题。

blocks.html_en: No amount of memory can retrieve facts that were never observed.

sentences.en: No amount of memory can retrieve facts that were never observed.
sentences.zh: 再多的记忆也无法检索出从未观察到的事实。

blocks.html_en: The challenge is not simply to preserve a known set of premises and derive their consequences. It is to reason under uncertainty about hidden causes.

sentences.en: The challenge is not simply to preserve a known set of premises and derive their consequences.
sentences.zh: 挑战不仅仅是保留一组已知的前提并得出其结果。

sentences.en: It is to reason under uncertainty about hidden causes.
sentences.zh: 它是在不确定的情况下对隐藏原因进行推理。

blocks.html_en: Informal reasoning also depends heavily on concepts whose meanings are unstable.

sentences.en: Informal reasoning also depends heavily on concepts whose meanings are unstable.
sentences.zh: 非正式推理也很大程度上依赖于含义不稳定的概念。

blocks.html_en: Words such as “fair,” “successful,” “responsible,” “harmful” or “intelligent” do not possess the exactness of mathematical variables. Their meaning depends on culture, goals and context.

sentences.en: Words such as “fair,” “successful,” “responsible,” “harmful” or “intelligent” do not possess the exactness of mathematical variables.
sentences.zh: “公平”、“成功”、“负责任”、“有害”或“聪明”等词语不具备数学变量的精确性。

sentences.en: Their meaning depends on culture, goals and context.
sentences.zh: 它们的含义取决于文化、目标和背景。

blocks.html_en: A model can remember every sentence in a discussion while still misunderstanding what the participants mean.

sentences.en: A model can remember every sentence in a discussion while still misunderstanding what the participants mean.
sentences.zh: 模型可以记住讨论中的每句话，但仍然会误解参与者的意思。

blocks.html_en: The same applies to political analysis, historical interpretation, business strategy and psychological judgment. In these domains, the central problem is often not working-memory capacity. It is identifying the correct causal model when the evidence is incomplete and ambiguous.

sentences.en: The same applies to political analysis, historical interpretation, business strategy and psychological judgment.
sentences.zh: 这同样适用于政治分析、历史解释、商业策略和心理判断。

sentences.en: In these domains, the central problem is often not working-memory capacity.
sentences.zh: 在这些领域中，核心问题通常不是工作记忆容量。

sentences.en: It is identifying the correct causal model when the evidence is incomplete and ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 当证据不完整且不明确时，它正在识别正确的因果模型。

blocks.html_en: A larger notebook helps, but it does not solve the fundamental problem.

sentences.en: A larger notebook helps, but it does not solve the fundamental problem.
sentences.zh: 更大的笔记本会有所帮助，但并不能解决根本问题。

blocks.html_en: Mathematics is different because the reasoning environment is artificially constructed to make assumptions explicit and transformations verifiable.

sentences.en: Mathematics is different because the reasoning environment is artificially constructed to make assumptions explicit and transformations verifiable.
sentences.zh: 数学则不同，因为推理环境是人为构建的，以使假设明确且变换可验证。

blocks.html_en: Mathematical answers can often be checked.

sentences.en: Mathematical answers can often be checked.
sentences.zh: 数学答案经常可以被检查。

blocks.html_en: A solution to an equation can be substituted back into the original expression. A proposed identity can be evaluated numerically. A computer program can test hundreds of cases. A formal proof assistant can verify whether every inference follows from accepted rules.

sentences.en: A solution to an equation can be substituted back into the original expression.
sentences.zh: 方程的解可以代回原始表达式。

sentences.en: A proposed identity can be evaluated numerically.
sentences.zh: 可以对提议的身份进行数值评估。

sentences.en: A computer program can test hundreds of cases.
sentences.zh: 一个计算机程序可以测试数百个案例。

sentences.en: A formal proof assistant can verify whether every inference follows from accepted rules.
sentences.zh: 正式的证明助理可以验证每个推论是否都遵循公认的规则。

blocks.html_en: This creates an ideal environment for AI.

sentences.en: This creates an ideal environment for AI.
sentences.zh: 这为人工智能创造了理想的环境。

blocks.html_en: The model can use its context not only to produce a solution but also to record alternative approaches, identify contradictions and correct previous mistakes.

sentences.en: The model can use its context not only to produce a solution but also to record alternative approaches, identify contradictions and correct previous mistakes.
sentences.zh: 该模型不仅可以利用其上下文来产生解决方案，还可以记录替代方法、识别矛盾并纠正以前的错误。

blocks.html_en: In less formal domains, feedback is much weaker.

sentences.en: In less formal domains, feedback is much weaker.
sentences.zh: 在不太正式的领域，反馈要弱得多。

blocks.html_en: A persuasive historical explanation may be impossible to verify conclusively. A business strategy may not reveal whether it was correct until years later. A psychological interpretation may remain permanently uncertain.

sentences.en: A persuasive historical explanation may be impossible to verify conclusively.
sentences.zh: 有说服力的历史解释可能无法得到最终证实。

sentences.en: A business strategy may not reveal whether it was correct until years later.
sentences.zh: 商业策略可能要到几年后才能揭示它是否正确。

sentences.en: A psychological interpretation may remain permanently uncertain.
sentences.zh: 心理学解释可能永远不确定。

blocks.html_en: In such fields, a long and coherent argument can still be completely wrong.

sentences.en: In such fields, a long and coherent argument can still be completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 在这些领域，冗长而连贯的论证仍然可能是完全错误的。

blocks.html_en: Mathematics rewards systems that can generate, store and verify explicit intermediate states. These are precisely the abilities that context windows, scratchpads, code execution and formal verification amplify.

sentences.en: Mathematics rewards systems that can generate, store and verify explicit intermediate states.
sentences.zh: 数学奖励可以生成、存储和验证显式中间状态的系统。

sentences.en: These are precisely the abilities that context windows, scratchpads, code execution and formal verification amplify.
sentences.zh: 这些正是上下文窗口、暂存器、代码执行和形式验证所增强的能力。

blocks.html_en: Some researchers would object to describing a context window as working memory.

sentences.en: Some researchers would object to describing a context window as working memory.
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员反对将上下文窗口描述为工作记忆。

blocks.html_en: They have a point.

sentences.en: They have a point.
sentences.zh: 他们说得有道理。

blocks.html_en: Human working memory is not merely a storage buffer. It involves attention, inhibition, continuous updating and the active manipulation of internal representations.

sentences.en: Human working memory is not merely a storage buffer.
sentences.zh: 人类工作记忆不仅仅是一个存储缓冲区。

sentences.en: It involves attention, inhibition, continuous updating and the active manipulation of internal representations.
sentences.zh: 它涉及注意力、抑制、持续更新和内部表征的主动操纵。

blocks.html_en: A language model’s context is more passive. Previous tokens remain fixed. The model cannot literally return to an earlier line and replace it. It generates new tokens conditioned on the existing record.

sentences.en: A language model’s context is more passive.
sentences.zh: 语言模型的上下文更加被动。

sentences.en: Previous tokens remain fixed.
sentences.zh: 以前的令牌保持固定。

sentences.en: The model cannot literally return to an earlier line and replace it.
sentences.zh: 该模型实际上无法返回到较早的生产线并替换它。

sentences.en: It generates new tokens conditioned on the existing record.
sentences.zh: 它根据现有记录生成新的令牌。

blocks.html_en: The most accurate description may therefore be augmented symbolic working memory.

sentences.en: The most accurate description may therefore be augmented symbolic working memory.
sentences.zh: 因此，最准确的描述可能是增强的符号工作记忆。

blocks.html_en: The model has weaker private mental memory than a human in some respects, but vastly greater explicit memory in others.

sentences.en: The model has weaker private mental memory than a human in some respects, but vastly greater explicit memory in others.
sentences.zh: 该模型在某些方面的私人心理记忆比人类要弱，但在其他方面却比人类的外显记忆要强得多。

blocks.html_en: Humans are better at silently maintaining a small internal state. AI is better at operating over an enormous written record.

sentences.en: Humans are better at silently maintaining a small internal state.
sentences.zh: 人类更擅长默默地维持一个小的内部状态。

sentences.en: AI is better at operating over an enormous written record.
sentences.zh: 人工智能更擅长对大量的书面记录进行操作。

blocks.html_en: For mathematics, the second ability may often be more valuable.

sentences.en: For mathematics, the second ability may often be more valuable.
sentences.zh: 对于数学来说，第二种能力往往可能更有价值。

blocks.html_en: Formal reasoning does not require every relevant state to remain private. On the contrary, mathematics improves when assumptions and intermediate steps are made explicit.

sentences.en: Formal reasoning does not require every relevant state to remain private.
sentences.zh: 正式推理并不要求每个相关状态都保持私有状态。

sentences.en: On the contrary, mathematics improves when assumptions and intermediate steps are made explicit.
sentences.zh: 相反，当假设和中间步骤明确时，数学就会得到改善。

blocks.html_en: The apparent weakness of AI—its tendency to “think out loud”—becomes an advantage when the domain itself is built from written symbols.

sentences.en: The apparent weakness of AI—its tendency to “think out loud”—becomes an advantage when the domain itself is built from written symbols.
sentences.zh: 当人工智能领域本身是由书面符号构建时，人工智能的明显弱点——它“大声思考”的倾向——就变成了优势。

blocks.html_en: This leads to a broader question: what does it mean to say that AI is “better at mathematics” than humans?

sentences.en: This leads to a broader question: what does it mean to say that AI is “better at mathematics” than humans?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个更广泛的问题：说人工智能比人类“更擅长数学”是什么意思？

blocks.html_en: Imagine giving two people the same mathematical problem.

sentences.en: Imagine giving two people the same mathematical problem.
sentences.zh: 想象一下给两个人同样的数学问题。

blocks.html_en: One must solve it entirely in their head. The other receives unlimited paper, perfect notes, instant access to every previous calculation, the ability to try several approaches in parallel and a machine that checks each result.

sentences.en: One must solve it entirely in their head.
sentences.zh: 人们必须在头脑中完全解决这个问题。

sentences.en: The other receives unlimited paper, perfect notes, instant access to every previous calculation, the ability to try several approaches in parallel and a machine that checks each result.
sentences.zh: 另一个则收到无限的纸张、完美的笔记、即时访问之前的每一次计算、并行尝试多种方法的能力以及检查每个结果的机器。

blocks.html_en: If the second person wins, we would not necessarily conclude that the second person possesses greater raw mathematical intelligence. We might instead conclude that the second person had a much better cognitive architecture for the task.

sentences.en: If the second person wins, we would not necessarily conclude that the second person possesses greater raw mathematical intelligence.
sentences.zh: 如果第二个人获胜，我们不一定会得出第二个人拥有更高的原始数学智力的结论。

sentences.en: We might instead conclude that the second person had a much better cognitive architecture for the task.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们可能会得出这样的结论：第二个人对这项任务有更好的认知架构。

blocks.html_en: The same caution should apply when comparing humans and AI.

sentences.en: The same caution should apply when comparing humans and AI.
sentences.zh: 在比较人类和人工智能时也应同样谨慎。

blocks.html_en: AI systems are trained on enormous quantities of mathematical material. They can generate many possible solutions, use code, consult tools and preserve long reasoning traces.

sentences.en: AI systems are trained on enormous quantities of mathematical material.
sentences.zh: 人工智能系统接受了大量数学材料的训练。

sentences.en: They can generate many possible solutions, use code, consult tools and preserve long reasoning traces.
sentences.zh: 他们可以生成许多可能的解决方案、使用代码、查阅工具并保留长推理痕迹。

blocks.html_en: Their performance is therefore the product of several factors: mathematical knowledge, reasoning ability, memory capacity, search, and verification.

sentences.en: Their performance is therefore the product of several factors: mathematical knowledge, reasoning ability, memory capacity, search, and verification.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们的表现是几个因素的产物：数学知识、推理能力、记忆能力、搜索和验证。

blocks.html_en: We tend to focus on reasoning because it is the most philosophically exciting component. But memory may be doing much more of the work than we realize.

sentences.en: We tend to focus on reasoning because it is the most philosophically exciting component.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于关注推理，因为它是哲学上最令人兴奋的组成部分。

sentences.en: But memory may be doing much more of the work than we realize.
sentences.zh: 但记忆所起的作用可能比我们意识到的要多得多。

blocks.html_en: The working-memory hypothesis produces clear predictions.

sentences.en: The working-memory hypothesis produces clear predictions.
sentences.zh: 工作记忆假说给出了明确的预测。

blocks.html_en: AI’s advantage should be largest on problems that involve:

sentences.en: AI’s advantage should be largest on problems that involve:
sentences.zh: 人工智能的优势应该在涉及以下问题上最大：

blocks.html_en: • many interacting constraints;

sentences.en: many interacting constraints;
sentences.zh: 许多相互作用的约束；

blocks.html_en: many interacting constraints;

sentences.en: many interacting constraints;
sentences.zh: 许多相互作用的约束；

blocks.html_en: • long calculations;

sentences.en: long calculations;
sentences.zh: 长时间的计算；

blocks.html_en: long calculations;

sentences.en: long calculations;
sentences.zh: 长时间的计算；

blocks.html_en: • extensive case analysis;

sentences.en: extensive case analysis;
sentences.zh: 广泛的案例分析；

blocks.html_en: extensive case analysis;

sentences.en: extensive case analysis;
sentences.zh: 广泛的案例分析；

blocks.html_en: • repeated reference to previous results;

sentences.en: repeated reference to previous results;
sentences.zh: 重复参考以前的结果；

blocks.html_en: repeated reference to previous results;

sentences.en: repeated reference to previous results;
sentences.zh: 重复参考以前的结果；

blocks.html_en: • exact symbolic bookkeeping;

sentences.en: exact symbolic bookkeeping;
sentences.zh: 精确的象征性簿记；

blocks.html_en: exact symbolic bookkeeping;

sentences.en: exact symbolic bookkeeping;
sentences.zh: 精确的象征性簿记；

blocks.html_en: • large bodies of formal definitions.

sentences.en: large bodies of formal definitions.
sentences.zh: 大量的正式定义。

blocks.html_en: large bodies of formal definitions.

sentences.en: large bodies of formal definitions.
sentences.zh: 大量的正式定义。

blocks.html_en: Its advantage should be smaller on problems that depend primarily on one short conceptual leap.

sentences.en: Its advantage should be smaller on problems that depend primarily on one short conceptual leap.
sentences.zh: 对于主要依赖于短暂概念跳跃的问题，它的优势应该较小。

blocks.html_en: A brilliant mathematician may still outperform AI when the crucial challenge is finding an entirely new representation of a problem. Once that representation has been found, however, AI may be superior at exploring all its consequences.

sentences.en: A brilliant mathematician may still outperform AI when the crucial challenge is finding an entirely new representation of a problem.
sentences.zh: 当关键挑战是找到问题的全新表示形式时，一位杰出的数学家仍然可能胜过人工智能。

sentences.en: Once that representation has been found, however, AI may be superior at exploring all its consequences.
sentences.zh: 然而，一旦找到了这种表征，人工智能可能会更擅长探索其所有后果。

blocks.html_en: The hypothesis also predicts that reducing a model’s usable context or preventing it from writing intermediate steps should disproportionately damage performance on long mathematical tasks.

sentences.en: The hypothesis also predicts that reducing a model’s usable context or preventing it from writing intermediate steps should disproportionately damage performance on long mathematical tasks.
sentences.zh: 该假设还预测，减少模型的可用上下文或阻止其编写中间步骤会不成比例地损害长期数学任务的性能。

blocks.html_en: Conversely, expanding a human’s external memory—with clear notation, diagrams, software and structured notes—should narrow part of the gap.

sentences.en: Conversely, expanding a human’s external memory—with clear notation, diagrams, software and structured notes—should narrow part of the gap.
sentences.zh: 相反，通过清晰的符号、图表、软件和结构化笔记来扩展人类的外部记忆，应该会缩小部分差距。

blocks.html_en: The fairest comparison may therefore not be AI against a human thinking unaided. It may be AI with its tools against a human with equally powerful external memory and verification systems.

sentences.en: The fairest comparison may therefore not be AI against a human thinking unaided.
sentences.zh: 因此，最公平的比较可能不是人工智能与人类独立思考的比较。

sentences.en: It may be AI with its tools against a human with equally powerful external memory and verification systems.
sentences.zh: 它可能是人工智能及其工具对抗具有同样强大的外部存储器和验证系统的人类。

blocks.html_en: The rise of mathematical AI is often described as a triumph of machine intelligence over human intelligence.

sentences.en: The rise of mathematical AI is often described as a triumph of machine intelligence over human intelligence.
sentences.zh: 数学人工智能的兴起通常被描述为机器智能对人类智能的胜利。

blocks.html_en: That interpretation may be premature.

sentences.en: That interpretation may be premature.
sentences.zh: 这种解释可能还为时过早。

blocks.html_en: AI certainly appears to be learning better reasoning strategies. It may eventually develop forms of mathematical intuition that equal or exceed our own.

sentences.en: AI certainly appears to be learning better reasoning strategies.

blocks.html_en: The physicist Eugene Wigner, who knew both John von Neumann and Albert Einstein, wrote that no one he had encountered possessed a mind as “quick and acute” as von Neumann’s. Von Neumann could absorb vast amounts of information, follow extraordinarily complicated arguments and move between mathematical fields with astonishing speed. Yet Wigner still regarded Einstein’s understanding as deeper, more penetrating and more original. Von Neumann may have had the greater raw intellectual processing capacity, but Einstein was more likely to reconceptualize the problem itself.

content_html_zh:
当人工智能系统解决了一个困难的数学问题时，通常的解释是它变得更加聪明。

也许它吸收了数以百万计的数学例子。 也许强化学习教会了它更好的推理策略。 也许它正在开始发展出类似真正数学直觉的东西。

所有这些解释可能都有一定道理。 但他们忽略了一个更简单的可能性：

人工智能拥有比人脑大得多的工作记忆。

或者，更准确地说，它可以访问巨大的外部符号工作空间，该工作空间执行人类工作记忆执行的许多功能。

这种差异在数学中可能尤其重要。

人类数学家只能同时记住少量不熟悉的元素。 人工智能模型可以将整个问题陈述、数百个中间方程、几种废弃的方法、定义、约束和早期结论保留在其上下文窗口内。

我们通常将由此产生的表现解释为卓越推理的证据。 但其中一些可能反而反映了人类推理最重要的生物学限制之一的消除：我们极其有限的工作记忆能力。

工作记忆是一种心理系统，使我们能够在短时间内保存和操纵信息。

解方程时，必须记住每个变量代表什么，已经执行了哪些操作以及当前目标是什么。 在证明过程中，您可能需要跟踪假设、中间引理、例外和多种可能的情况。

人类的工作记忆非常有限。

它的确切容量取决于任务和信息的组织方式，但从日常经验来看，一般限制是显而易见的。 尝试在头脑中将两个三位数相乘。 底层操作很简单。 困难主要来自于在执行额外计算时必须保留部分结果。

把数字写下来可以改变问题。

纸并不会让你变得更聪明。 它可以扩展您的有效工作记忆。

同样的原理也适用于更高层次的数学。 数学家使用符号、草稿纸、图表和先前写下的引理不仅是为了传达解决方案，而且是为了使推理在认知上成为可能。

专家通过“分块”进行补偿。 新手看到一长串符号。 专家会识别熟悉的结构并将其视为单个概念对象。 这使得在相同的生物工作记忆限制内可以容纳更多的信息。

但分块并不能消除限制。 它只是压缩信息。

人工智能模型面临着截然不同的约束。

工作记忆对于数学的重要性不仅仅是理论上的。 从人与人之间的差异就可以看出。

工作记忆与一般智力密切相关，这提出了一个明显的问题：它是否独立预测数学表现，或者仅仅是智商的另一种不完美的衡量标准？

多项研究表明，它的贡献超出了传统的情报措施。 例如，Alloway 和 Passolunghi (2011) 检查了儿童的工作记忆、语言能力和数学技能。 他们发现工作记忆测量对数学表现做出了明显的贡献，而不是简单地再现数学和一般语言能力之间的关联。

在一项单独的为期六年的纵向研究中，阿洛韦和阿洛韦（2010）测量了五岁时的儿童，然后在六年后检查了他们的学业成绩。 即使在分析中纳入了智商之后，早期的工作记忆表现也能预测后来的识字和算术能力。 事实上，工作记忆比研究中使用的智商测量更能预测后期的学业成绩。

Blankenship 及其同事（2015）类似地报告说，在统计控制智商和年龄后，工作记忆解释了数学流畅性和计算的独特变化。 Friso-van den Bos 及其同事（2013）进行的一项大型荟萃分析也发现，小学研究中的工作记忆和数学之间存在一致的关系，尽管这种关系的强度根据工作记忆和所测量的数学任务的类型而有所不同。

这些发现不应被夸大。 工作记忆和智力有很大重叠，统计控制无法将它们完美地隔离为独立的心理机制。 证据也不意味着商业训练工作记忆一定会带来智力或数学的巨大进步。

然而，狭义的结论仍然很重要：在具有相似测量智力的儿童中，掌握、更新和操纵信息的能力的差异仍然预示着数学表现的差异。

这为理解人工智能提供了重要线索。 如果人类的数学表现在一定程度上受到工作记忆瓶颈的限制，那么为机器提供巨大的符号工作空间就会改变比赛的性质。 机器在数学上可能显得更加智能，部分原因是它较少受到抑制人类表现的认知限制的约束。

现代语言模型可以同时处理大量的标记序列。 该序列可能包括原始问题、定义、示例、中间计算和模型自己的早期推理。

上下文窗口与人类工作记忆不同。 更好地理解它是一个巨大的外部笔记本，加上一个不完善的搜索和使用其中所写内容的系统。

这种区别很重要。

人类拥有一种活跃的内部记忆。 我们可以默默地选择一个数字，将其牢记在心，对其进行转换并用新值替换它，而无需说或写任何内容。

标准语言模型在维持这种私密的、不断更新的心理状态方面要弱得多。 它们最稳定的记忆形式通常是已经生成的标记序列。

如果模型写道：

x=6

后来写道：

x+3=9,

这些陈述仍然在上下文中。 模型可以在生成下一步时再次关注它们。

因此，它的推理常常是外化的。 文本不仅仅是完整思维过程的报告。 文本是推理发生机制的一部分。

人类在使用草稿纸时也会做类似的事情。 主要区别在于规模。

一个没有帮助的人可能很难同时保持五个不熟悉的条件处于活动状态。 人工智能可以以明确的形式保存数十或数百个它们。

这并不意味着长上下文中的每个项目都可以完美检索。 模型可能会忽略相关信息、分心或忘记细节。 公布的上下文长度与完全可用的内存不同。

然而，潜在能力的差异是巨大的。

上下文窗口的优势并非在每种推理中都同样有用。

这对数学尤其重要，因为数学推理可以非常好地转化为明确的符号。

几乎数学问题的每个相关元素都可以写下来：

  • 假设；
  • 定义；
  • 已知方程；
  • 目前的目标；
  • 结果已经证明；
  • 已消除的案件；
  • 每个步骤保持有效的条件。

一旦写入，该信息就保持稳定。

如果 (x) 在证明开始时被定义为整数，则除非证明明确更改定义，否则它仍然是整数。 严格的不平等不会因为情绪、背景或解释的变化而逐渐变成非严格的不平等。

数学符号旨在减少歧义。

这使得数学几乎完全适合通过大型文本工作空间运行的智能。

考虑一个要求求解器记住以下内容的问题：

  • n 为奇数；
  • p 是素数；

  • x≠0

并且论证的一个分支已经产生了矛盾。

人类可能理解基本策略，但在确定 x≠0 之前先除以 x。 错误不一定是由于缺乏智力造成的。 可能是记账失败。

人工智能可以重申每个阶段的主动约束：

我们假设 (n) 为奇数、(p) 为素数且 (x≠0)。

上下文成为推理状态的分类账。

许多困难的数学问题在开始时就包含了深刻的见解，但随后也包含了大量不那么光鲜亮丽的工作：扩展表达式、检查案例、通过转换携带条件以及确保最终结论与每个早期假设兼容。

机器不需要比人类拥有更深刻的洞察力来获得优势。 它可能只是在完成一长串操作的同时能够更好地保留问题的整个状态。

数学是高度综合性的。

证明通常可以表示为：

A → B → C → D

如果每一步都是有效的并且链条被准确保存，那么结论如下。

较大的工作空间允许模型在丢失线程之前构建更长的链。

这很重要，因为问题的难度不仅仅取决于每个步骤的难度。 它还取决于必须协调多少步骤。

一个人可能完全有能力理解 100 步论证中的每一个局部推论，但仍然无法在没有帮助的情况下生成整个论证。 这个问题超出了人维持全局结构的能力。

人工智能可以通过写下几乎所有东西来进行潜在的补偿。

这可以解释为什么额外的“思考时间”通常会提高模型性能。 更多的计算允许系统产生更多的中间状态，检查替代分支并保留部分结论。

看似更深层次的思考有时可能是在更大的笔记本中进行的更广泛的搜索。

现在将数学问题与社会问题进行比较：

为什么玛丽亚突然不再回复我的消息了？

更大的上下文窗口可能允许人工智能检查多年的通信。 它可以识别语气、时间和词汇的变化。

但决定性的信息可能仍然缺失。

也许玛丽亚很生气。 也许她很忙。 也许她病了。 也许她丢了手机。 也许她是在回避一个不相关的问题。

再多的记忆也无法检索出从未观察到的事实。

挑战不仅仅是保留一组已知的前提并得出其结果。 它是在不确定的情况下对隐藏原因进行推理。

非正式推理也很大程度上依赖于含义不稳定的概念。

“公平”、“成功”、“负责任”、“有害”或“聪明”等词语不具备数学变量的精确性。 它们的含义取决于文化、目标和背景。

模型可以记住讨论中的每句话，但仍然会误解参与者的意思。

这同样适用于政治分析、历史解释、商业策略和心理判断。 在这些领域中，核心问题通常不是工作记忆容量。 当证据不完整且不明确时，它正在识别正确的因果模型。

更大的笔记本会有所帮助，但并不能解决根本问题。

数学则不同，因为推理环境是人为构建的，以使假设明确且变换可验证。

数学答案经常可以被检查。

方程的解可以代回原始表达式。 可以对提议的身份进行数值评估。 一个计算机程序可以测试数百个案例。 正式的证明助理可以验证每个推论是否都遵循公认的规则。

这为人工智能创造了理想的环境。

该模型不仅可以利用其上下文来产生解决方案，还可以记录替代方法、识别矛盾并纠正以前的错误。

在不太正式的领域，反馈要弱得多。

有说服力的历史解释可能无法得到最终证实。 商业策略可能要到几年后才能揭示它是否正确。 心理学解释可能永远不确定。

在这些领域，冗长而连贯的论证仍然可能是完全错误的。

数学奖励可以生成、存储和验证显式中间状态的系统。 这些正是上下文窗口、暂存器、代码执行和形式验证所增强的能力。

一些研究人员反对将上下文窗口描述为工作记忆。

他们说得有道理。

人类工作记忆不仅仅是一个存储缓冲区。 它涉及注意力、抑制、持续更新和内部表征的主动操纵。

语言模型的上下文更加被动。 以前的令牌保持固定。 该模型实际上无法返回到较早的生产线并替换它。 它根据现有记录生成新的令牌。

因此，最准确的描述可能是增强的符号工作记忆。

该模型在某些方面的私人心理记忆比人类要弱，但在其他方面却比人类的外显记忆要强得多。

人类更擅长默默地维持一个小的内部状态。 人工智能更擅长对大量的书面记录进行操作。

对于数学来说，第二种能力往往可能更有价值。

正式推理并不要求每个相关状态都保持私有状态。 相反，当假设和中间步骤明确时，数学就会得到改善。

当人工智能领域本身是由书面符号构建时，人工智能的明显弱点——它“大声思考”的倾向——就变成了优势。

这就引出了一个更广泛的问题：说人工智能比人类“更擅长数学”是什么意思？

想象一下给两个人同样的数学问题。

人们必须在头脑中完全解决这个问题。 另一个则收到无限的纸张、完美的笔记、即时访问之前的每一次计算、并行尝试多种方法的能力以及检查每个结果的机器。

如果第二个人获胜，我们不一定会得出第二个人拥有更高的原始数学智力的结论。 相反，我们可能会得出这样的结论：第二个人对这项任务有更好的认知架构。

在比较人类和人工智能时也应同样谨慎。

人工智能系统接受了大量数学材料的训练。 他们可以生成许多可能的解决方案、使用代码、查阅工具并保留长推理痕迹。

因此，它们的表现是几个因素的产物：数学知识、推理能力、记忆能力、搜索和验证。

我们倾向于关注推理，因为它是哲学上最令人兴奋的组成部分。 但记忆所起的作用可能比我们意识到的要多得多。

工作记忆假说给出了明确的预测。

人工智能的优势应该在涉及以下问题上最大：

  • 许多相互作用的约束；
  • 长时间的计算；
  • 广泛的案例分析；
  • 重复参考以前的结果；
  • 精确的象征性簿记；
  • 大量的正式定义。

对于主要依赖于短暂概念跳跃的问题，它的优势应该较小。

当关键挑战是找到问题的全新表示形式时，一位杰出的数学家仍然可能胜过人工智能。 然而，一旦找到了这种表征，人工智能可能会更擅长探索其所有后果。

该假设还预测，减少模型的可用上下文或阻止其编写中间步骤会不成比例地损害长期数学任务的性能。

相反，通过清晰的符号、图表、软件和结构化笔记来扩展人类的外部记忆，应该会缩小部分差距。

因此，最公平的比较可能不是人工智能与人类独立思考的比较。 它可能是人工智能及其工具对抗具有同样强大的外部存储器和验证系统的人类。

数学人工智能的兴起通常被描述为机器智能对人类智能的胜利。

这种解释可能还为时过早。

人工智能显然正在学习更好的推理策略。 它最终可能会发展出相当于或超过我们自己的数学直觉。

但它目前的一些优势可能更为平淡无奇。

人类大脑是在严格的限制下进化的。 它的工作记忆有限，会变得疲倦，丢失中间结果，并且难以协调一长串不熟悉的符号。

人工智能不受相同架构的约束。

它可以将推理转化为文本，并将该文本用作巨大的外部认知工作空间。 数学由于其精确性和符号结构，是这种优势最容易转化为卓越表现的领域。

因此，人工智能在数学上击败人类的真正原因可能并不像我们想象的那么神秘。

也许最具启发性的比较不是人工智能和普通人之间的比较，而是两种截然不同的天才之间的比较。

认识约翰·冯·诺依曼和阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦的物理学家尤金·维格纳写道，他遇到的没有人拥有像冯·诺依曼那样“快速而敏锐”的思维。 冯·诺依曼可以吸收大量信息，遵循极其复杂的论点，并以惊人的速度在数学领域之间移动。 但维格纳仍然认为爱因斯坦的理解更深刻、更透彻、更独创。 冯·诺依曼可能拥有更强的原始智力处理能力，但爱因斯坦更有可能重新概念化问题本身。

当今的人工智能看起来更像是第一组能力的机器放大版本，而不是第二组能力。 它速度极快、范围广泛，能够保存和操作大量显式信息。 它可以搜索多种可能性，记住一长串的推论，并以无人辅助的人类无法比拟的规模执行形式推理。 但这并不一定意味着它具有爱因斯坦式的深度：抛弃公认的框架、识别隐藏的概念错误并发明一种看待现实的全新方式的能力。

这个类比不应该太过分。 冯·诺依曼本人是一位极具原创性的思想家，而不仅仅是一位快速计算器。 但维格纳的区别抓住了一些重要的东西。 目前，人工智能在数学上击败人类的方式可能不是通过像爱因斯坦那样思考，而是通过将类似于冯·诺依曼的速度和广度与几乎无限的笔记本相结合。

当人工智能不仅能够比人类更快地解决现有问题时，我们将达到下一个伟大的门槛。 当人工智能能够认识到问题的表述不正确并发明一种从根本上更好的理解方法时，这一目标就会实现。
